items.title: Pixel Tag, Google’s $30 Android-ready answer to Apple’s AirTag, is now available
items.summary: Google's Pixel Tag lets you track lost items with your Android device, similar to Apple's AirTag.
items.content:
Google’s answer to Apple’s AirTag, the Google Pixel Tag , goes on sale starting Tuesday, allowing Android users to track items like their keys, wallet, or bag using their smartphone’s built-in Find Hub.

First announced in August , the $29.99 device takes cues from the AirTag and other lost-item finders by offering connectivity via Bluetooth and ultra-wideband for precision finding. This lets Android device owners, including Pixel Watch wearers, locate their missing items using a combination of visual distance and directional guidance.

Plus, the tag has a built-in speaker to play a chime that helps you locate your item if nearby. (Or, if you’ve lost your phone, you can press the button on the Pixel Tag twice to ring it, too.) You can choose between three different levels of loudness in the settings within the Find Hub, with the maximum volume around 80 decibels.

Though the Pixel Tag serves the same purpose as an AirTag, Google has opted for a different design. Instead of a small, round device, like Apple’s, the Pixel Tag is slimmer and more elongated.

Spec-by-spec, the Pixel Tag is 1.1-inches wide, compared to the AirTag’s 1.26 inches. As the Pixel Tag is oval-shaped, it’s 1.8-inches high from top to bottom. Thickness-wise, the Pixel Tag clocks in at a depth of 0.2 inches, compared with the AirTag’s 0.31 inches (which Apple calls its height). The slimness of the device might make it more appealing for some, particularly if they’re adding the tag to a small item, like a keychain.

The device weighs just 0.4 oz, with the battery included.

Unlike Apple, Google opted for a physical button you can press on the tag, which makes it more obvious how it’s meant to work.

Google didn’t originally say that the Pixel Tag included NFC when it announced the device in August. NFC is used by Apple’s AirTag to aid people who find lost items, as they can tap the side of the tag to launch a webpage that displays the owner’s contact information. Google uses the tap gesture to instead connect the user to the device’s settings.

Meanwhile, for lost items that are not nearby, the Pixel Tag relies on Google’s crowdsourced network of over a billion Android devices globally. The network, similar to competitive offerings from Apple and Tile, taps into the connectivity provided by other Android devices, which can identify and share the location of the lost item back to its owner. This location information is displayed on a map inside the Find Hub app.

While the person who found the item can’t tap it, as with NFC-enabled devices, Pixel Tags that are put into “Lost” mode will be able to share the owner’s email, number, and a short message so the person who finds the tag can contact you. When the tag comes back into range of the user’s phone, the item is automatically marked as found.

The Pixel Tag’s location can also be shared with up to 10 people in the Find Hub app, which could be useful for shared items like the family car keys, which multiple people might rely on.

Meanwhile, the device itself is made from stainless steel and features IP67 water and dust resistance (maximum depth of 1 meter up to 30 minutes). It pairs with devices running Android 9 or newer via Fast Pair technology.

The Pixel Tag comes in two shades: silver and a pale green, and can be bought individually or in a four-pack for $99.99.

Alongside the launch, the company Bellroy is debuting its own keychain cases in a variety of colors and styles, which will also be sold on the Google Store.

Post updated after publication to note that the Pixel Tag now supports NFC, which was a surprise addition not mentioned at the time of its announcement.

items.summary: Article URL: https://lwn.net/SubscriberLink/1102549/acbc92e00cee3a3f/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50443824 Points: 256 # Comments: 114
items.content:
The dock that he was trying to support is a Dell device that connects to a system via USB 3 and allows users to connect multiple monitors and other devices to their computer. It provides its DisplayLink Manager (DLM) software for Linux for the devices via an APT repository for Ubuntu.

The company only provides DLM software in binary form, and only for x86-based platforms. The software is proprietary, but the company does maintain an open-source, out-of-tree kernel module that is included with DLM, the Extensible Virtual Display Interface (EVDI) project. It provides a driver that's compatible with Linux DRM and allows users to manage their docked displays with standard tools used for display settings, such as xrandr or GNOME and KDE Plasma's utilities.

A short article explains why the company has not released source code for DLM: the software uses a proprietary graphics technology called DL3 to create a compressed stream of the various channels (e.g., USB, DisplayLink video, audio) over a communication channel (USB 3 in this case) and decode it again for output to the user's devices.

Unfortunately, the vendor-supplied software did not work well for Lothian. I spoke and chatted with him via Signal while writing this article; he said that the driver kept crashing under Linux, so he decided to use his Claude subscription to try to develop a new driver and support software.

He posted the first patch series for Vino—his Rust-based DRM/KMS driver—to the kernel's dri-devel list as an RFC on June 17. Lothian noted that it was in an incomplete state, and asked for help with a blocker that he had run into trying to communicate with the dock's control plane. " If you have knowledge of the DisplayLink DL3 control-plane engagement sequence, or ideas for isolating a whole-bus timing/ordering property a per-channel diff cannot see, help would be very welcome. " He received feedback from a few developers, including guidance from Danilo Krummrich to rework the driver to use the Rust KMS bindings , but no advice specific to the problem he was trying to solve.

Lothian also opened an issue on the EVDI GitHub repository on June 17. It explained the work he'd done so far, outlined the approach in trying to reverse-engineer the DL3 protocol, provided links to his GitHub repository with the Vino code, and asked for clarification on a few issues. There was no reply to his issue.

He also reached out to Łukasz Spintzyk of Synaptics directly by email; his correspondence with the company between July 5 and October 7 is available in this PDF compiled by Lothian . He noted that he had found a few bugs in EVDI and opened a pull request (that went unreviewed for several months), and also asked for assistance where he was blocked on Vino. On July 20, he received a reply, not from Spintzyk, but from Michal Lukaszek of Synaptics:

The reason I'm writing is that DisplayLink is not an open standard. The protocol, codec, and other technologies used by DisplayLink devices are proprietary to Synaptics and are protected by a substantial portfolio of patents in a number of jurisdictions, including the UK.

From what you've published, it appears that the VINO project is progressing beyond interoperability work and toward implementing technology that we believe is covered by those patents. While many developers understandably focus on avoiding copyrighted source code, patent law is different. An independently written or clean-room implementation does not necessarily avoid patent infringement if it implements patented inventions.

Lukaszek said it was entirely possible that Lothian was unaware of the " intellectual property landscape surrounding DisplayLink ", so he wanted to make him aware now rather than " have the situation become more formal later ". Lothian lives in Scotland and has a ".co.uk" email address, which explains why the email made reference to the UK.

On August 17, Andrew Bateman, an assistant general council of intellectual property for Synaptics, sent a cease-and-desist notice . The letter stated that Lothian had not " substantially responded " to Lukaszek's communication, and had continued with " public statements and further development activities ". It included an appendix with a list of 125 patents that " cover fundamental aspects of DisplayLink's architecture and operation ", but did not specify which patents might be infringed by the work.

Synaptics included a list of eight demands it expected immediate compliance with, including ceasing development of " any software or other implementation that infringes any Synaptics patent ", withdrawing submissions of materials " made to Linux kernel maintainers, mailing lists, code-hosting platforms, package maintainers, distributions, or any other person or organization ", and to identify in writing every location " in which the relevant materials have been published, submitted, stored, or distributed ". It also demanded that he provide Synaptics with a signed confirmation, by August 28, that he had complied with its demands.

Lothian, instead, posted version three of his Vino work for the DisplayLink docks to the dri-devel list on August 26. He said that the previous two versions had " never lit a panel ", but the new work could control three generations of DL3 docks without any vendor software. There were no substantive reviews of the patch set posted to the list, though there were some automated reviews from Sashiko.

On August 27, Lothian responded to Bateman and asked him to elaborate on the patents that Synaptics thought were being infringed. " A claim chart mapping the relevant claims to the relevant code would make it much easier for me to understand and properly respond to your concerns. "

Modern Web Guidance is a set of skills that embed web platform expertise, best practices, and browser compatibility data directly into your coding agents. It helps to steer your coding agents away from legacy patterns, and instead toward solutions that harness the power and capabilities of the modern web platform.

Stewarded by the Google Chrome, Microsoft Edge, Mozilla Firefox, and MDN teams, alongside the web development community.

Documentation · Eval Dashboard · Source Code · Report an Issue

This command runs an interactive wizard to install Modern Web Guidance. See Alternative Installation Methods below.

Coding agents often default to older patterns because LLM training data contains vast amounts of legacy code. This often leads them to generate bloated JavaScript for tasks that now have native, high-performance web platform solutions.

Even if a model knows an API exists, it often lacks the density of real-world, modern implementation patterns required for production-ready code.

Modern Web Guidance bridges this gap. Our skill's CLI returns targeted, expert-curated guidelines directly into your agent's context window, focusing on:

We cover the past several years of the web platform's new features, all the way up to the cutting edge. The guides are designed to be token-efficient ; we run evals enabling us to prune lowest-common-denominator content that models already know.

Smooth visual states (View Transitions, entry/exit animations, parallax scroll, CSS scrollbar-color ).

Modern layout systems (container queries, subgrid , modern color spaces like oklch , text-wrap tuning, and line-height trimming).

Speed optimizations (instant preloading, Interaction to Next Paint (INP) diagnostics, and scheduling tasks via scheduler.yield ).

Native components (Anchor Positioning for tooltips, Popover API, dialogs, :user-invalid validation, and auto-sizing fields).

Important considerations (screen reader and keyboard operability, content navigation and discoverability).

Local client models (native translation, summarization, and language detection APIs).

View an example: the navigation-drawer guide .

Configure Origin Trial and volatile feature opt-ins for a repository with an optional .mwgrc JSON file in your project root (or ~/.mwgrc as a user-level fallback), which you can commit to share across your team:

Note: We use npx to ensure the content doesn't go stale, but the CLI works offline, completely private and local. The npm package is self-contained, with no extra dependencies to ensure both low-latency and supply-chain security.

If you installed the skill using npx modern-web-guidance@latest install , you can update with: npx modern-web-guidance@latest update .

Otherwise, consult your agent's documentation for updating plugins and skills.

We developed a robust eval harness to ensure that the content is empirically proven and continuously calibrated so AI agents write better code. We run automated evaluations using a closed-loop validation pipeline:

Explore full per-agent and per-guide breakdowns on the Eval Dashboard .

You can customize which skill packs are installed using the --choose flag:

Google collects anonymous usage information to improve the tool's reliability, relevance, and performance. Collected information includes installation counts, the calling agent name, guide retrieval IDs, and CLI tool search queries generated by the agent (e.g. "dark mode scrollbar color-scheme"). Raw user prompts are not collected. You can inspect what is collected in modern-web.ts .

Found a bug, outdated pattern, or missing web platform feature? Open an issue or see CONTRIBUTING.md in the source repository ( GoogleChrome/modern-web-guidance-src ) .

Huge thanks to everyone who has contributed!

Portions of the documentation in this project are derived from MDN Web Docs by Mozilla Contributors and W3C , WHATWG , and IETF specifications.

items.content:
ChatGPT’s new AI agents represent companies and can help with things like comparison shopping.

ChatGPT is going to let you chat with verified “Business Agents” that represent a brand to help you with things like comparison shopping. The feature, available first to “eligible” e-commerce and online service businesses in the US, is launching as part of a suite of business-focused features in ChatGPT being announced today in beta .

You can start talking with a Business Agent if a business that has created one appears in a response from ChatGPT. While chatting with a custom agent, you can ask about a business’s offerings and ask follow-up questions, like asking about differences between two different products. Businesses can specify a Business Agent’s instructions and provide business context so that the agent knows how to respond.

Chats with Business Agents will be clearly labeled and separate from your main ChatGPT conversation, OpenAI says. To help people know that they’re talking with an agent that actually represents the business, companies will be able to claim their organization and get verified through a feature called Business Hub. (OpenAI isn’t sharing specifics about its verification methods because there are different methods for different businesses, VP of monetization Benji Shomair said in a press briefing.) Business Hub will also let companies see insights such as mentions in ChatGPT responses and top “discovery topics” where their business pops up.

“Today’s announcement is an early step in bringing businesses more deeply into ChatGPT,” OpenAI says in a blog post. “We’re starting with the foundations: accurate business information, useful insights and conversations that help people make informed decisions.” As things evolve, “we’ll explore more ways for businesses to connect with customers — directly or through agents and in ChatGPT and beyond. Our goal is to make ChatGPT more useful for people making decisions, and give businesses new ways to participate and grow.”

items.title: Git security vulnerabilities announced
items.summary: Git is releasing updates addressing six security vulnerabilities affecting recursive clones, reference handling, merges, binary patches, and imports. Here is what users need to know. The post Git security vulnerabilities announced appeared first on The GitHub Blog .
items.content:
Today, the Git project is releasing new versions to address six security vulnerabilities. These include arbitrary code execution when recursively cloning a malicious repository, writes to unintended files, and memory corruption when processing merges or binary patches.

The fixes are included in Git 2.56.1 , with backports to Git 2.55.1, 2.54.1, 2.53.1, 2.52.1, 2.51.3, and 2.50.2. We recommend updating to Git 2.56.1 or the patched release for your maintenance series, and updating any applications that bundle Git.

Git checks paths before writing files into a working tree, including rejecting paths that would overwrite its own repository metadata. However, an integer truncation in Git’s index handling can cause an extremely long path to pass validation under one name and then be written using a shorter name.Collapse comment

An attacker can use this discrepancy to replace a submodule’s .git file with a symbolic link pointing to a directory containing malicious configuration or hooks . When Git subsequently uses that directory, it can execute attacker-controlled code during a recursive clone.

The fix rejects extremely long index entry paths before their lengths can be truncated.

When cloning an empty repository using Git protocol v2, the server can advertise a HEAD symref pointing to an unborn branch (one that has no commits yet). Git did not validate the symref’s target before storing it locally.

A malicious server can supply a name containing path-traversal components. With the files reference backend, a later operation that updates the branch can write outside the intended reference directory.

Git now validates the advertised target before accepting it. The release also validates other reference names and symbolic-reference targets received through protocol v2.

When stripping GPG signatures from a message, Git assumed there would be at most two signatures. A specially crafted message containing more than two signatures can cause Git to write past the end of a fixed-size stack array.

This can be triggered by merging a tag containing more than two signatures, causing memory corruption and a potential denial of service. Hosting services that perform these merges on behalf of users can also be affected.

The fix removes the fixed-size array and handles messages with any number of signatures.

Git rejects patches larger than approximately 1 GiB because its patch application code cannot safely handle larger inputs. However, this check only considered the size of the patch as supplied.

Binary patches are compressed and encoded, so a relatively small patch can expand beyond that limit. A crafted patch can bypass the input-size check and cause an out-of-bounds read, crashing Git.

Git now also checks the declared uncompressed size before processing a binary patch.

Git’s merge machinery calculates how much memory it needs for a merge result before writing the output. That calculation can overflow when the result is very large, including when many conflicts are combined with a large conflict-marker-size attribute.

The overflow can cause Git to allocate a buffer that is too small, then write outside it, corrupting heap memory. This affects applications and hosting services that use Git to merge untrusted content, as well as local merges.

The fix uses size-appropriate types and checked arithmetic, rejecting merges whose output size cannot be represented safely.

git fast-import reads a stream of commands to build a repository. Some commands can access files outside the repository, so Git already restricts them when they appear in an untrusted input stream.

Three additional features lacked that protection. The rewrite-submodules-from and rewrite-submodules-to features can read arbitrary files, potentially exposing their contents through error messages. The export-pack-edges option can create files or append data to existing files.

These features are now rejected when supplied through the input stream unless the caller explicitly enables --allow-unsafe-features . Only enable that option when you trust the program generating the stream.

Alongside these fixes, the release adds overflow checks to related index entry allocations during checkout and tree processing. These checks complement the path-length limits above, preventing allocation sizes from being truncated or overflowing before Git copies a path into memory.

Updating is the most effective way to protect against these vulnerabilities. Install a patched version from your operating system or Git distributor, and update applications that include their own copy of Git. Administrators should also update Git installations used by automation and services that process repositories on behalf of users.

If you cannot update immediately, clone only from trusted servers and avoid recursive clones of untrusted repositories. Avoid merging untrusted content or tags, or processing binary patches or fast-import streams from untrusted sources. These precautions do not replace installing the fixes.

Get an updated version of Git >

items.title: Anthropic launches Claude Meetings to turn workplace discussions into plans and tasks
items.summary: As participants talk, Claude can draft the plan being discussed, map out a timeline on a whiteboard, answer questions in the meeting chat, and access connected work apps to retrieve information, such as last year's figures.
items.content:
Anthropic announced new workplace features on Tuesday, including Claude Meetings, which brings Claude into video calls to begin working on tasks while participants are still talking. The company also unveiled Claude Whiteboards and Claude Sheets.

The launch of Anthropic’s new productivity-focused features comes just a few weeks after OpenAI unveiled a series of workplace tools that allow users to collaborate with ChatGPT to do things like visualize company information and create presentations, as both companies compete to turn their products into office suites of sorts to take on Microsoft and Google. Meta is also joining the competition with its Muse AI agent, which can build mini-apps on the fly to help users complete specific tasks.

With Claude Meetings, teams can add Claude to a video call as a visible participant. Claude then follows the conversation and gets to work on tasks in real time. As participants talk, it can draft the plan being discussed, map out a timeline on a whiteboard, answer questions in the meeting chat, and access connected work apps to retrieve information, such as last year’s figures. After the call, the meeting notes, action items, and other materials Claude created are available in claude.ai.

The work that comes out of a meeting usually starts after everyone hangs up, but with this new feature, teams can turn discussions into actions in real time, Anthropic says.

Claude identifies itself as a meeting participant and posts a notice in the meeting chat. It won’t join calls with external guests unless authorized by an admin, and will automatically leave if an external guest joins.

Claude Meetings is launching in beta on Team and Enterprise plans. At launch, it works with Google Meet, with support for additional plans expected to follow.

As for Claude Whiteboards, Anthropic describes the feature as a collaborative board where teams can talk through a plan and have Claude turn it into an organized visual workspace with timelines and deadlines.

The company notes that many people already brainstorm with Claude, but that in order to share their results with others, they would have to copy-paste them somewhere else. Now, a team can work directly with Claude on the same board in real time.

When the brainstorm is done, Claude can turn the board into a doc or a slide deck. Additionally, Whiteboards also work inside Claude Meetings, so the board builds while people talk, Anthropic says.

Claude Whiteboards is available in beta on paid plans, on web, desktop, and mobile.

The company also launched Claude Sheets, which lets teams create and collaboratively edit spreadsheets with Claude. A team can ask it to build a campaign tracker or hiring budget, and Claude will then generate a working spreadsheet.

Anthropic says Claude handles the initial setup of trackers and budgets, while allowing teams to continue refining and updating the same spreadsheet. Each spreadsheet can include multiple tabs, formulas, formatting, and dropdown menus. Claude also makes edits directly in cells alongside the team, and outlines each change so users can see what it did.

Claude Sheets is available in beta on paid plans, on web, desktop and mobile.

Anthropic also announced that Claude Data, formerly known as Claude Dashboards, is now generally available. The feature connects Claude to systems that companies use to keep their numbers, like a data warehouse or CRM. Users can ask questions, and Claude responds with dashboards, written data stories, or narrated videos.

Additionally, the company announced interactive connectors that open the full version of apps like Adobe, Atlassian, and HubSpot inside Claude. Anthropic notes that teams can now open these apps directly alongside their Claude conversations and ask the assistant to work within them, essentially bringing existing workflows into the same workspace.

items.title: Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang’s affair with alleged Chinese spy: a timeline
items.summary: The affair could have ramifications for national security as the U.S. and China race to develop the most advanced AI infrastructure.
items.content:
Nvidia co-founder CEO Jensen Huang has never been as flashy or controversy-prone as AI leaders like OpenAI’s Sam Altman or SpaceXAI’s Elon Musk. Now, the 63-year-old industry kingpin has admitted that he cheated on his wife of 40 years in an affair that could have ramifications beyond Huang’s personal life and potentially impact national security.

United States officials believe that Huang’s likely romantic interest, Megaspeed executive Alice Huang, is a Chinese spy who has been feeding information back to Beijing. (Alice Huang, a Chinese citizen, is of no relation to Jensen Huang.)

Megaspeed, a Singapore-based AI infrastructure company, had reportedly purchased $4.8 billion in Nvidia chips over the last two years. The U.S. and Singapore have both previously investigated Megaspeed over suspicions that the firm was illegally sharing chips with China.

The U.S. and China are embroiled in a fierce technological arms race to build the most advanced AI infrastructure, which could shape each country’s economic future, military prowess, and capacity for innovation. Nvidia is valuable in this competition as one of the world’s largest makers of AI chips, which are essential for accelerating AI development. But as an American company, Nvidia faces government restrictions on the sale of its most powerful chips to Chinese entities.

As the controversy unfolds, we are organizing the most relevant events into a reverse-chronological timeline to keep you up to date.

The Nvidia CEO pulled out of upcoming speaking engagements at the ElevenLabs Summit and Anthropic CEO Forum.

Alice Huang and her family reportedly built a network of companies in China and Singapore to acquire Nvidia chips, including founding a Chinese company called Shanghai Century Litong. Founded in 2023, it became a Nvidia preferred cloud partner giving it priority access to chips, the Information reported . The Info reported that Shanghai Century Litong. facilitated buying $7.5 billion worth of Nvidia’s chips, including banned chips.

Nvidia’s head lawyer, Tim Teter, intervened in a 2025 US government probe surrounding the suspected smuggling of AI chips by Megaspeed International, Bloomberg reported . Teter contacted Commerce Under Secretary Jeffrey Kessler asking questions about whether the Trump administration played a role in detaining Alice Huang.

In early 2025, Alice Huang and a business partner sought China-based investors for an Asian data center, promising they had no problem in securing GPUs, the Financial Times reported.

On Sunday night, President Trump weighed in on Huang’s controversy and showed support for the Nvidia CEO.

“I have not spoken to him about it. I just know he’s a fine person, but you never know what’s going on,” Trump said.

When asked if Huang should remain chief of Nvidia , Trump said, “I think so. Oh yeah, sure.”

Jensen Huang wrote in a letter to Nvidia employees — which was also published as a press release — that he cheated on his wife.

“I owe my family and all of you an apology,” Huang told his company. “I was unfaithful to my wife. My actions hurt her and our children. There is no excuse for what I did. I am deeply sorry.”

Huang did not mention Alice Huang by name in the message, but linked his infidelity to “the national security concerns raised in news reports.”

“Nvidia’s Board of Directors has initiated an independent investigation. I support the investigation and will cooperate fully. I love our country and our company. I am committed to protecting Nvidia and supporting America’s national security. I am proud and grateful to be an American,” Huang wrote.

Nvidia shares slid over 5% the following day.

Three Republican congressmen — Chairman John Moolenaar of the House Select Committee on China, Chairman Brian Mast of the House Foreign Affairs Committee, and Chairman Rick Crawford of the House Permanent Select Committee on Intelligence — sent a request to Huang for a closed-door joint briefing with their three committees.

“Recent reports raise significant national security concerns regarding the [People’s Republic of China]’s access to sensitive U.S. technology and information,” the chairmen wrote . “The issue of PRC infiltration and access to cutting-edge U.S. technology is core to the investigative work of our three committees this Congress. It is vital that Congress determines the extent to which U.S. national security has been placed at risk.”

U.S. officials had been investigating Alice Huang and Megaspeed for more than a year when the New York Times broke the story in late October that the two executives also had a close relationship.

A Nvidia spokesperson denied that this relationship was something out of the ordinary.

“Jensen’s interactions with Ms. Huang are not unusual or unexpected. Meetings with customers are part of a CEO’s job; Jensen talks with thousands of customer executives every year,” Nvidia spokesperson John Rizzo said. He added that “if the U.S. government believes that any person is a threat to American industry, it would let us know.”

U.S. officials circulated a secret memo among policymakers which warned that Megaspeed’s Alice Huang, who had a relationship with Jensen Huang, was a spy for China’s Ministry of State Security. This memo was not public knowledge until it was later reported by the New York Times.

Secretary of State Marco Rubio supervised the drafting of the memo.

Around the same time, per the New York Times’ report , U.S. President Donald Trump was briefed about intelligence findings that possible Chinese spy Alice Huang had formed a close relationship to Jensen Huang. Trump did not act on this information.

The Nvidia CEO, an ally of Trump , has repeatedly advocated for the U.S. government to let Nvidia expand its business in China.

items.title: Sundrop turns your endless baby photos into recaps, time lapses, and more — without AI
items.summary: Sundrop is a new iPhone app that uses Apple's on-device AI to help parents rediscover their favorite photos and create keepsakes without uploading images to the cloud.
items.content:
New parents take a lot of pictures of their children, but those photos often end up languishing in photo galleries, never to be seen again after the initial snap and share.

A new app, Sundrop , aims to make those pictures more useful by turning them into weekly recaps, highlights, time lapses of the child growing up, and other cute scenes, like putting the child’s photo on a magazine cover or a rookie card.

While Google Photos and Apple Photos already provide extensive tools to organize and manage photos, Sundrop is taking aim at a particular niche: parents with a new baby (usually their first!) who take an overwhelming number of photos and want to do more with those pictures.

The app was developed over the past few months by the same team behind the read-it-later app, Matter: Ben Springwater, Sky Lan, and Rob Mackenzie (all dads themselves).

Notably, Sundrop claims it is designed to be private, and processes all photos locally on the device it is installed on. To make this possible, Sundrop taps into Apple’s Vision framework and on-device Core ML (machine learning) models instead of uploading photos to a cloud server or some other hosted AI service.

Both of the child’s parents can use Sundrop together by linking their accounts, which allows the app to sync their shared photos via Apple’s iCloud service. This feature, the company says, means the pictures aren’t sent to any external servers it runs.

In addition, the team notes that no generative AI is used in the creation of its scenes or highlights.

This differentiates it from many photo-editing apps on the market, including Google’s, which are increasingly tapping generative AI to create new versions of your photos.

To find highlights and recaps, Sundrop scans pictures in the parents’ respective Camera Rolls on their iPhones, skipping things like screenshots or duplicates. It then creates highlights or fun scenes, which it calls “drops.”

One of these is a recap of the week every Sunday, announced as a Lock Screen notification. Others can put two siblings side-by-side at the same age, generate a time-lapse series of photos or a video of a kid growing up, or cut out a photo of the child and place it into a layered template.

Parents can also manually edit the photos Sundrop uses to make its creations, or use the app to automatically organize the best photos into galleries with other similar shots.

The app costs $39.99 per year, and offers a week-long free trial. The annual plan also includes Family Sharing, so only one parent needs to purchase it.

items.title: Blender 5.3 released with Gaussian Splat support
items.summary: Article URL: https://www.blender.org/download/releases/5-3/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50442426 Points: 409 # Comments: 57
items.content:
Welcome native 3D Gaussian Splats support to Blender 5.3!

Import them as point clouds, experiment with Geometry Nodes, preview them in Workbench, and render them natively with EEVEE or Cycles.

3D Gaussian Splats are commonly used to reconstruct 3D scenes from photos or videos. They consist of many small, soft, transparent blobs that combine to represent complex geometry and shading.

Blender can now import Gaussian Splats from PLY , SPZ , and glTF files, store them as point clouds, process them with Geometry Nodes, and render them in EEVEE, Cycles, and Workbench (solid mode).

Gaussian splats are represented as point clouds, using a new type to tell them apart and with special attributes:

By default, a 3D Gaussian Splat is rendered using an emissive shader. The radiance attribute provides access to the resolved radiance of the splat at the current shading point.

There is rudimentary support for making the splat relightable by replacing the Emission node with a hard surface BSDF such as Diffuse BSDF.

Performance is still being optimized. Rendering may produce inaccuracies due to differences between the sRGB space used by most Gaussian Splat authoring tools and Blender’s linear color space, particularly in areas with low opacity and high radiance.

The Principled BSDF now supports Dispersion !

Turn ordinary glass and diamonds into beautiful little rainbows by splitting white light into its colorful components.

With Dispersion in the Transmission panel, the Principled BSDF can now reproduce the characteristic rainbow effect seen in glass and gemstones. This corresponds to OpenPBR v1.1.1.

Roughness anisotropy is also now supported by the Glass BSDF and the transmission component of the Principled BSDF. It behaves just like anisotropy for specular reflections.

Blender 5.3 integrates DLSS 4.5 Ray Reconstruction as a new denoiser, delivering cleaner images faster by upscaling and reusing samples from previous frames.

Think Cycles looks with EEVEE responsiveness.

NVIDIA DLSS brings near-final render quality to the viewport, making lighting and look development faster and more responsive while virtually eliminating flickering between frames during animation playback.

Find it in the Denoise panel under Render properties, Sampling.

DLSS denoising requires NVIDIA driver version 620 or newer.

Blender 5.3 brings native support for NVIDIA RTX Spark devices running Windows 11, including memory optimizations.

Material Lighting nodes allow authoring how the Material reacts to Lights.

This can, for example, be used for toon and stylized shading, but also for complex physical effects like iridescence.

Per-light data, evaluation, and shadow information are now available in the Shader Editor, giving you more control over how materials respond to individual scene lights.

Four new nodes and two that received a “Light” mode/space:

EEVEE can now render panoramic cameras, supporting all types of projections, from equirectangular and cubemap formats to various fisheye models and mirror ball.

The current implementation has a few limitations: depth of field, raytracing, and volumetric temporal reprojection in the viewport are not yet supported.

You can now stack Effects on your scene just like you would modifiers or constraints.

Applying compositing effects has never been easier.

Choose from built-in effects such as Bloom , Chromatic Aberration , Film Grain , and Vignette , as well as effects from online asset libraries or your own custom compositor node groups.

Internally, each effect is its own node group, with its output passed on to the next effect.

You can further customize effects at any time in the Compositor editor.

17 Geometry Nodes are now supported in the Compositor, bringing a range of new capabilities across bundles , math and logic, and utility operations.

This includes bundle support with Get Bundle Item , Store Bundle Item , Combine Bundle , Typed Bundle , and Separate Bundle .

Math and logic nodes such as Boolean Math , Compare , Float to Integer , Integer Math , Matrix SVD , Combine Transform , and Separate Transform . Plus utility nodes including Hash Value , Random Value , Is Viewport , Import Text , and Bone Info .

Playback is now up to 2x faster on GPU, particularly when playing back EXR sequences.

The interactive compositor now supports playback caching . It can be enabled from the sidebar, Options panel.

Anisotropic Kuwahara is now up to 10x faster on Apple GPUs, 2x faster on NVIDIA GPUs, and 25-30% on CPU.

Blender splash artwork source files are available for you to play with!

Until now, Blender’s preferences (such as asset libraries) were shared across all projects, and it was up to users to keep related files and resources organized.

Blender now supports projects, giving you a way to group related files, share resources, and manage settings across an entire project, whether you’re working alone or as part of a team.

Projects support custom variables that can be used throughout a project, such as a character’s name or a frequently used file path.

Per-project asset libraries and color management configurations are also supported. You can even set up a custom splash screen for your project, providing quick access to its files and other recent projects.

Add-ons and other extensions per-project will follow in future Blender versions.

Projects are entirely optional, most of the time you’ll probably work without one.

Asset libraries can now be shared as extensions! Just like add-ons or themes.

Browse hundreds of public domain assets available on the Extensions platform via the Get Extensions tab and install them directly from within Blender.

Create and share your own asset library extension. Optionally, access can be controlled via authentication tokens .

Draw Mode now has its own selection tools: Tweak , Lasso , Box , and Circle . Select strokes and adjust them right where you draw.

items.title: Gemini 4 Carbon is now available
items.content:
Developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers can now try our latest frontier model.

SVP, Google DeepMind and Chief AI Architect, Google

Your browser does not support the audio element.

Today, we’re making Gemini 4 Carbon available to developers, enterprises, scientists, and consumers. Carbon is our strongest model with frontier performance in cybersecurity capabilities and long-horizon agentic workflows across complex knowledge work, software engineering, and scientific reasoning.

Two weeks ago , we released Carbon to a set of cybersecurity defenders via our Fairwind Program . Following our recent launch of Gemini 4 Argon , Carbon pushes the frontier even further. Argon remains the ideal choice for the majority of software engineering and knowledge work, while Carbon is built for tasks that test the limits of a model’s intelligence like complex, multi-step coding and debugging and open-ended scientific research and discovery — using more tokens than Argon to explore thoroughly, reason deeply, and run extended verification loops.

Across independent benchmarks designed to test model performance in real workflows, Carbon pairs frontier accuracy with practical production economics. It ranks #1 on CursorBench 4.0 , Perplexity’s WANDR , and Zapier’s AutomationBench at more than 2X lower cost per task compared to the next best external model.

To put Carbon’s capabilities to work on larger and complex projects, we’re previewing /swarm in Google Antigravity, turning a single prompt into a coordinated team of agents you can track in real time. Developers can assign Carbon to roles that demand the deepest reasoning, like architectural design, coordination, and auditing, while pairing it with faster, lighter models across parallel isolated workspaces and adversarial verifiers that test every change.

Across legal, finance, and enterprise operations, Gemini 4 Carbon combines frontier visual understanding, reasoning, and exhaustive retrieval to synthesize grounded insights across large sets of dense documents and data. It follows strict schemas and formatting to generate polished and precise spreadsheets, presentations, and reports.

Existing benchmarks don’t adequately capture how agents reason natively over dense files with charts, images, blueprints, schematics, and tables, so we partnered with Artificial Analysis to launch the new Multimodal Knowledge Agent (MKA) benchmark that tests a model’s multimodal performance in agentic workflows. Carbon ranks #2 while being more than 6X lower in average cost per task compared to the top performing model.

Using Google Antigravity’s new /swarm feature, a team of Gemini 4 Carbon agents turned historical photos and engineering plates into an interactive Three.js 3D exhibition of the Eiffel Tower's 1887–1889 construction from a single prompt.

With seven public City Council planning PDFs (206 extracted engineering drawing views) and a single prompt, a multi-agent Carbon team using Google Antigravity’s /swarm feature built an interactive 906K-triangle Three.js reconstruction of Google’s Platform 37 office across 10 overnight loops.

In Google Antigravity, Gemini 4 Carbon built an interactive multiscale textile visualizer based on an academic paper, modeling a virtual-fiber finite element framework with interactive 3D yarn meshes, 110-fiber polar tracking, and dynamic stress-strain curves with minimal prompting.

In pre-release evaluations, Carbon matched the performance of the best model tested on deep financial research on Hebbia’s E2E Financial Agentic evaluation, and ranked at the top out of 23 frontier model configurations on Balyasny Asset Management’s General Financial Intelligence benchmark, spanning legal expertise, agentic tool use and execution, coding and data engineering, and perception and context understanding.

Carbon performs exceptionally well on engineering tasks that require multi-agent collaboration like multi-package migrations, cross-subsystem root-cause investigations, and complex architectural redesigns. For web app development, it runs build-and-verify loops, recovers from errors, and checks both its code and the rendered UI to produce complete, working applications. Stronger visual design, spatial reasoning, and attention to environmental detail also carry over to 3D game development and creative coding.

Using Google Antigravity’s /swarm feature, Carbon built an open-world 3D game where you explore Google’s Mountain View campus as a pelican riding a GBike — coordinating subagents to model 3D assets in Blender from Omni and Nano Banana references, build the browser game in Three.js with WebGL shaders, and pair procedural Web Audio sound effects with Lyria music. Try the live app .

Paired with improved front end taste and motion design skills in Google Antigravity, Carbon reimagined the Google Merchandise Store in two prompts, proposing five art direction concepts and generating all-new product imagery with Nano Banana 2.1. Try the live app and Gemini front end design skill .

Starting from a video reference generated with Gemini Omni in Google Antigravity, built a cinematic multi-shot underwater Atlantis scene. The pipeline modeled procedural ruins, volumetric caustic lighting, and water simulation in Blender before converting the full environment to Three.js for real-time browser rendering.

Using a multi-agent loop in Google Antigravity, Carbon reconstructed a playable c. 1780 Stein-Schule fortepiano with 61-key escapement physics from CAD drawings and X-ray radiographs and placed it in a 3D model of the Royal Conservatory of Music's Koerner Hall in Toronto with seat-specific spatial acoustics. Try the live app .

items.title: Smart home devices should work without the internet
items.summary: Article URL: https://docodethatmatters.com/home-automation-overnight-success/ Comments URL: https://news.ycombinator.com/item?id=50441707 Points: 630 # Comments: 225
items.content:
AI;DR: I wrote the first draft, AI helped me edit and rewrite it, and I made the final pass. The rules, setups, and talks are my own.

TLDR; Nothing core in my house depends on a vendor’s server. If the internet goes down, the house keeps running. That’s been rule one for about ten years, and my other rules came out of it. This post has the rules, then both talks I’ve given on home automation, slide by slide.

My Nest integration worked until Google broke the API. That’s the failure I plan around now. The talks have a few more: a Samsung fridge showing a TLS certificate error on its own screen, and a Camp Chef grill controller that needs Wi-Fi to show you the temperature.

Everything that matters runs on hardware I own. That’s Tasmota on ESP boards, an MQTT broker, and Node-RED on a Raspberry Pi. I do use some cloud services, mostly Alexa and a few AWS ones. Alexa is just another way to flip a switch. If it’s down, the wall switches and the wall dashboard still work.

From the first talk, restated in the second:

Added after year five, once more people lived in the house:

The build I get asked about most is the Tasmota sprinkler controller . It’s in both talks, and so is the garage door setup, which has been running about as long.

Nobody needs any of this. I like building things that just work in the background, and each automation is a small puzzle.

Everything talks to a cloud now: phones, laptops, thermostats, locks. Those clouds may or may not be up when you need them, so know what you’re signing up for before you plug something in.

Most people start here: a thermostat, a plug, a lock. Each has its own app and account.

Every device lands somewhere on this triangle. A cloud camera is cheap and easy, and it costs you privacy. A switch I flash myself takes longer to set up, but I can hook it into anything. I figure out where a device lands before I buy it.

Someone (often me) automates a light, then has to tape the wall switch on so the smart bulb keeps power. If a switch in a room ever did nothing, this is why.

The better fix is an in-wall Wi-Fi switch. The switch still works like a normal switch and I can still automate it. It’s more work to install than a smart plug, but nobody has to change their habits.

Rule one: if the internet goes down, my lights still turn on.

It’s never done. Rooms get used differently, people move in and out, new devices show up. Whatever you build has to be cheap to change.

The garage cooling flow starts from a manual trigger and checks if the door is closed. Then it opens the door, waits, and turns on the fan. If cooling is already running, it just sends a notification. Small flow, but it has kept the garage from baking more than once.

The door sensor and reed switch both report into a transform step that sets a global garage-closed flag and logs to Grafana. Below that is the chart from a few real days: 21 opens, with spikes showing when each one happened. It’s easy to skip reporting/alerting. This can alert me if the garage was left open, which is useful when I accidentally leave it open.

Four scheduled triggers all hit the same pump. It’s easy to end up with automations fighting over one device, so every so often I check whether they still make sense together.

I’ve broken all of these plenty of times, so they’re more like guidelines.

Three ways to do “event in, action out.” Node-RED is my main tool. Alexa routines and IFTTT-style applets cover the stuff I don’t want to build myself.

A Sonoff Mini fits inside the fireplace wiring, and the dashboard or Alexa can flip it. A fake fire you can turn on by voice is a good party trick.

The whole sprinkler build: the relay and ESP module in the enclosure, the 3D board render, the Tasmota UI with BME280 sensor readings, the Node-RED schedule feeding the pump, and the finished PCB layout. The sprinkler post has the full writeup, including why I picked Tasmota over custom firmware. It’s a bit hacky but I love it :D

The whole talk in five lines. The one I break most is the first, don’t introduce a new way while removing the old one, and I regret it every time. The last one stops me from breaking the others for no good reason. “I was in a hurry” doesn’t count.

That was talk one. Most of the “memorable automations” later broke in some new way or got replaced, so there’s a sequel.

Enough time passed between the talks that I had a new list of problems.

More devices means more decisions made without me. It’s a little unsettling but mostly harmless.

Same slide as before, with more icons.

Everyone else is dealing with this too: a fridge showing a TLS certificate error, a grill controller that needs Wi-Fi to show the temperature, and a note taped to a pole about an internet-connected printer someone forgot to log out of.

The same rules from talk one, worded a bit tighter, since part of the audience hadn’t seen the first talk.

The rules stayed the same, but what they had to survive got harder.

My setup assumed one person lived in the house. When that changed, I had to patch a single-user system into a multi-user one. The next few slides are how that went.

More people meant more foot traffic and more keys, and longer trips away meant things could fail with nobody around to notice. A water flooding scare finally got me to take leak and presence detection seriously.

Same joke, new rules. The first set came after year one, these after year five.

These are rules 6 to 11 at the top of the post, written after the house went from one person to several.

Now the builds, my favorite part.

A motor and PVC pipe rig for outdoor lighting, a UV grow light clipped to a houseplant, and a UV strip under the cabinets for sanitizing.

Same sprinkler slide as talk one. It’s one of the few builds that never needed a rewrite.

FactoryTalk® View Machine Edition(ME) 애플리케이션용으로 제작된 PanelView Pro는 더 빠른 성능, 향상된 내구성 및 유지보수와 라이프사이클 관리를 간소화하는 모듈형 아키텍처를 결합하여 기존 애플리케이션의 손쉬운 마이그레이션 경로를 제공합니다.

Rockwell Automation introduces PanelView Pro to deliver high-performance visualization for modern manufacturing

제조기업이 노후화된 인프라를 현대화해야 한다는 압박이 커지면서, 많은 기업이 운영의 연속성을 유지하는 동시에 변화하는 사이버보안 및 규제 준수 요구사항을 균형 있게 맞추는 데 어려움을 겪고 있습니다. Human Machine Interface(HMI) 시스템을 업그레이드할 때는 종종 애플리케이션 재개발, 판넬 수정, 생산 가동 중단 시간이 필요합니다. PanelView Pro는 고객이 기존 FactoryTalk View ME 애플리케이션을 유지하면서 최신 하드웨어 플랫폼으로 전환할 수 있도록 하여 이러한 과제를 해결합니다.

"제조기업은 점점 더 까다로워지는 운영을 따라잡으면서 장기적인 현대화 목표를 지원할 수 있는 비주얼라이제이션 기술이 필요합니다."라고 로크웰 오토메이션의 시각화 및 자산 관리 부문 부사장 겸 총괄 매니저인 Angela Rapko는 말했습니다. "PanelView Pro는 고객이 현대적인 그래픽 터미널에서 기대하는 성능, 내구성, 유연성을 결합했으며, 모듈형 설계를 통해 유지보수를 간소화하고 기존 FactoryTalk View ME 투자 자산을 보호하는 데 도움을 줍니다."

PanelView Pro의 주요 기능은 다음과 같습니다.

"제조기업은 생산 연속성을 유지하면서 노후화된 HMI 인프라를 현대화하고, 사이버보안을 강화하며, 더 나은 생산 현장 가시성과 상황에 맞는 정보를 필요로 하는 AI 기반 운영에 대비할 수 있는 실질적인 방법이 필요합니다."라고 ARC Advisory Group의 부사장인 Craig Resnick은 말했습니다. "PanelView Pro는 더 높은 성능의 비주얼라이제이션, 향상된 내구성 및 애플리케이션 재사용을 지원하는 모듈형 아키텍처를 통해 이러한 우선순위를 해결합니다. 또한 FactoryTalk View ME에서의 마이그레이션을 간소화하고 기존 투자를 보호하는 데에도 도움을 줍니다. 이러한 라이프사이클 중심 접근 방식은 장기적인 복원력, 유지보수성 및 보다 정보에 기반한 운영 결정을 지원하는 동시에 현대화의 비용, 복잡성 및 운영 리스크를 줄이는 데 도움이 될 수 있습니다."

PanelView Pro는 로크웰 오토메이션의 비주얼라이제이션 포트폴리오의 일부로, 고객에게 FactoryTalk View ME 애플리케이션을 현대화할 수 있는 명확한 경로를 제공하며, 라이프사이클 관리를 단순화하고 시각화 솔루션 전반에 걸쳐 일관된 하드웨어 경험을 유지합니다. PanelView Pro는 2026년 4분기부터 고객에게 제공될 예정이며, 추가 모듈형 구성요소와 확장된 구성은 2027년 내에 순차적으로 제공될 예정입니다.

PanelView Pro에 대한 자세한 정보는 https://www.rockwellautomation.com/ko-kr/products/hardware/hmi/panelview-pro.html 에서 확인할 수 있습니다.

PanelView Pro란 무엇인가요? 로크웰 오토메이션의 PanelView Pro는 까다로운 산업용 애플리케이션을 위해 설계된 고성능 그래픽 터미널입니다. 이 제품은 빠른 처리 속도, 반응성이 뛰어난 그래픽, 향상된 사이버보안 기능, 그리고 유지보수와 라이프사이클 관리를 간소화하는 모듈형 아키텍처를 결합하고 있습니다. 또한 기존 FactoryTalk View ME 애플리케이션에 대해 간단한 마이그레이션 경로를 제공하여, 고객이 대대적인 재개발 없이도 현대화할 수 있도록 지원합니다.

PanelView Pro는 누구를 위해 설계되었나요? PanelView Pro는 가동 중단 시간, 엔지니어링 노력 및 운영 리스크를 최소화하면서 노후화된 HMI 인프라를 현대화하고자 하는 OEM, 시스템 통합업체 및 최종 사용자를 위해 설계되었습니다.

PanelView Pro는 어떤 문제를 해결합니까? 많은 제조기업이 노후화된 HMI 하드웨어를 교체해야 하지만, 애플리케이션 재개발, 판넬 재설계, 생산 가동 중단 시간에 대한 우려를 가지고 있습니다. PanelView Pro는 기존 FactoryTalk View ME 투자를 보존하면서 최신 하드웨어로 전환할 수 있도록 저비용 마이그레이션 경로를 제공합니다.

글로벌뉴스 입력 :2026/11/11 00:10

2026년 9월 21일 미국소비자기술협회가 PR 뉴스와이어(PR Newswire)를 통해 배포한 '테케드라 마와카나 웨이모 공동 CEO, CES 2027 기조연설자로 나선다' 보도자료에 변경 사항이 있음을 해당 기업으로부터 전달받아 알려드립니다. 행사 일시가 2027년 1월 5일(화) 오후 6시 30분(태평양 표준시, PST)으로 업데이트되었으며, 정정된 보도자료의 전체 내용은 다음과 같습니다:

웨이모, 자율주행 차량 호출 서비스의 미래 비전 공유

샌프란시스코 , 2026년 9월 22일 /PRNewswire/ -- 테케드라 마와카나(Tekedra Mawakana) 웨이모(Waymo) 공동 CEO가 CES 2027에서 기조연설에 나선다고 CES® 의 소유자이자 주최자인 미국소비자기술협회(Consumer Technology Association, CTA)® 가 발표했다. 웨이모는 기술이 새로운 호기심의 대상에서 일상생활의 필수품으로 진화하는 모습을 보여주는 대표적인 사례다. 웨이모의 자율주행 차량은 매주 운행 서비스를 50만 건 넘게 제공하고 있으며, 이미 사업 지역 내 도로 안전 개선에 기여하고 고령자와 이동에 제약이 있는 사람들이 직면한 현실적 문제에도 대응하고 있다.

Tekedra Mawakana, Co-CEO, Waymo

킨지 파브리치오(Kinsey Fabrizio) CTA 회장 겸 CEO는 "자율주행 차량은 출근을 할 때든 비행기를 타러 갈 때든 병원에 갈 때든 편리하고 이용이 간편하며 가성비도 좋다"며 "웨이모는 첨단 AI와 로보틱스를 통합해 모빌리티의 미래를 만들어가고 있다. 마와카나 CEO가 앞으로의 비전에 대해 어떤 이야기를 들려줄지 기대된다"고 말했다.

마와카나 CEO는 모빌리티의 미래를 만들어 가는 대표적 인물 중 한 명이다. 2019년부터 2021년까지 CTA 산업 리더 이사회(Board of Industry Leaders)에서 활동했다. 타임 100 AI(TIME 100 AI) 와 포브스 50 오버 50( Forbes ' 50 Over 50)에 선정된 바 있으며 기술과 리더십, 혁신의 교차점에 관해 꾸준히 의견을 발표해 왔다. 그의 활동과 영향력은 뉴욕타임스 (The New York Times), 배니티 페어(Vanity Fair) 를 비롯한 세계 주요 매체에서 소개되기도 했다.

마와카나 CEO는 "웨이모는 완전 자율주행 교통수단을 일상생활에 자연스럽게 녹아드는 서비스로 만들고 있다"며 "사람들이 목적지까지 더욱 안전하고 신뢰할 수 있는 방법으로 이동할 수 있는 서비스를 확대하고 있다. CES는 전 세계가 다음 단계의 기술을 직접 경험하는 곳이다. 웨이모와 함께라면 모빌리티의 미래를 상상하는 데 그치지 않고 실제로 호출할 수 있다"고 말했다.

웨이모는 세계에서 가장 신뢰받는 운전자가 된다는 사명을 바탕으로 매년 교통사고로 119만 명이 목숨을 잃는 긴급한 글로벌 위기에 대응하고 있다. 웨이모는 피로하거나 주의가 산만해지거나 운전 능력이 저하되지 않으면서도 연중무휴 24시간 이용할 수 있는 운전자를 개발해 한층 높은 안전 기준을 제시하고 있다. 마와카나 CEO는 CES 기조연설에서 해외 시장 확대와 차량단 진화 등을 추진하면서도 웨이모가 이러한 안전 기준을 어떻게 유지하고 있는지 자세히 설명할 예정이다.

게리 샤피로(Gary Shapiro) CTA 이사회 의장은 "웨이모는 교통을 더욱 안전하고 이용하기 쉬우며 효율적으로 만들고 있다"며 "마와카나 CEO의 리더십은 삶의 질을 높여주고 정책적 인사이트를 촉발하며 기술의 힘을 뒷받침하는 혁신을 잘 보여준다"고 말했다.

마와카나 CEO는 2027년 1월 5일 화요일 오후 6시 30분(미국 태평양 표준시) 베네시안(The Venetian)의 팔라초 볼룸(Palazzo Ballroom)에서 연설한다. 그는 앞서 CES 2025 리더스 인 테크놀로지 디너(CES 2025 Leaders in Technology Dinner) 에서도 연설한 바 있다.

웨이모는 1월 6일부터 9일까지 라스베이거스 컨벤션 센터 웨스트홀 내 부스 3741에서 만날 수 있다. 웨이모는 최근 미국 내 15번째 시장인 라스베이거스에서 처음으로 일반 승객을 받기 시작했으며, CES 참석자들에게 완전 자율주행 차량을 직접 경험할 기회를 제공할 계획이다.

자율주행 차량의 다음 단계는 어떤 모습일지 확인하기 좋은 기회다. 기조연설 무대에는 스텔란티스(Stellantis)도 참여한다. CES 2027 등록은 지금부터 할 수 있다.

CES® 소개 CES는 세계에서 손꼽히게 영향력 있는 기술 행사로, 획기적인 기술과 글로벌 혁신가들이 가능성을 입증하는 무대다. 세계 최대 브랜드들이 비즈니스를 펼치고 새로운 파트너를 만나며, 가장 뛰어난 혁신가들이 연단에 선다. 미국소비자기술협회가 소유하고 주최하며 기술 산업의 모든 영역을 아우른다. CES 2027은 1월 6일부터 9일까지 라스베이거스에서 열린다. 자세한 내용은 CES.tech 에서 확인할 수 있다. 소셜미디어 에서 CES를 팔로우해도 된다.

미국소비자기술협회(CTA)® 소개 북미 최대 기술 무역협회인 CTA는 기술 산업을 대표한다. 회원사는 스타트업부터 글로벌 브랜드까지 세계를 선도하는 혁신 기업으로 구성돼 있으며, 이들이 미국 내에서 지원하는 일자리만 해도 1700만개가 넘는다. CTA는 세계에서 손꼽히게 영향력 있는 기술 행사인 CES®를 소유하고 주최한다. 자세한 내용은 CTA.tech 에서 확인할 수 있다. @CTAtech 를 팔로우해도 된다.

30년 넘게 이어온 '그녀는 미를 타고났나봐(Maybe she's born with it)'가 모든 여성의 무한한 가능성을 기리는 메시지로 진화한다.

뉴욕 , 2026년 11월 10일 /PRNewswire/ -- 세계 1위* 메이크업 브랜드 메이블린 뉴욕(Maybelline New York)이 뷰티 업계에서 가장 널리 알려진 슬로건 가운데 하나인 자사의 대표 슬로건을 새롭게 개편해 앞으로 지속적으로 사용한다고 이날 발표했다. 1991년 처음 선보인 '그녀는 미를 타고났나봐. 메이블린을 쓰나봐(Maybe she's born with it. Maybe it's Maybelline)'는 새로운 시대에 맞춰 다음과 같이 재해석됐다.

The Beauty of Infinite Possibility, a global brand platform launching with Maybelline Global Brand Ambassador Miley Cyrus.

어쩌면. 우리는 미를 타고났나봐.(MAYBE. WE'RE BORN WITH IT.) 메이블린을 쓰나봐.(MAYBE. IT'S MAYBELLINE.)

새로운 슬로건은 메이블린의 마일리 사이러스(Miley Cyrus) 글로벌 브랜드 앰배서더와 함께 선보이는 글로벌 브랜드 플랫폼 무한한 가능성의 아름다움(The Beauty of Infinite Possibility)의 출범을 알린다.

30년 넘게 '그녀는 미를 타고났나봐'는 한 여성의 아름다움에 관한 질문을 던졌다. 새롭게 해석된 '어쩌면.'은 모든 여성과 이들이 앞으로 될 수 있는 모든 모습에 관한 선언이다. 마침표 하나가 질문을 무한한 가능성의 선언으로 바꾸고, '그녀'에서 '우리'로의 변화는 그 의미를 한 여성에서 모든 여성으로 확장한다. 이제 '어쩌면.'은 가능성을 뜻하며, 모든 여성은 그 가능성을 타고난다. 이는 메이크업이 불어넣을 수 있는 자신감과 자기표현의 자유를 통해 모든 여성이 내면의 가능성을 탐색하도록 이끄는 긍정적인 초대다.

오늘날 아름다움은 겉모습보다 스스로 어떤 기분을 느끼는지에 따라 정의되는 경향이 커지고 있다. 맥킨지&컴퍼니(McKinsey & Company)에 따르면 전 세계 소비자의 절반을 조금 넘는 비율이 아름다움이란 자신감을 느끼는 것이라고 답했다. 반면 남에게 매력적으로 보이거나 최대한 오래 젊어 보이는 것과 연결한 응답자는 약 26%였다.¹ 또한 2026년 유럽 소비자 조사에서는 79%가 메이크업이 외모를 가꾸는 것을 넘어 자신감을 느끼고 자신을 표현하는 데 도움이 된다고 답했다.² 이러한 결과는 메이크업이 자신감을 키우고 자기표현을 장려하며, 모든 연령대의 여성에게 자신의 다양한 면모를 탐색할 자유를 주는 역할을 할 수 있음을 보여준다.

메이블린에 이러한 변화는 브랜드의 유산을 자연스럽게 이어가는 과정이다. 110여 년 전 현대적 마스카라를 발명한 이래 메이블린은 전 세계 여성들이 뛰어난 성능의 메이크업 제품을 쉽게 접할 수 있도록 노력해 왔다. 끊임없이 새로운 모습을 만들어가는 도시 뉴욕에 뿌리를 둔 메이블린은 여성들과 함께 변화하며 새로운 시도와 개성, 자신을 표현할 자유를 장려해 왔다. 새로운 플랫폼은 이러한 유산을 이어가며 메이크업을 통해 여성들이 자신감을 키우고, 오늘의 자신을 표현하며, 내일 어떤 모습이 될 수 있을지 발견할 수 있다는 메시지를 전한다.

메이블린의 상드린 졸리(Sandrine Jolly) 글로벌 브랜드 사장 은 "메이블린은 메이크업이 자신을 새롭게 바라보고, 자신이 누구인지 표현하며, 원하는 모습으로 거듭날 수 있는 길을 열어준다고 믿는다. '어쩌면.'을 통해 우리의 유산을 이어가는 동시에, 전 세계 여성이 삶의 어느 단계에 있든 내면의 가능성을 탐색하도록 초대하고 있다. 메이크업은 일상에서 호기심을 불러일으키는 작은 불씨이자 '만약 해본다면?'을 '못 할 이유가 있겠어?'로 바꾸는 계기가 될 수 있다. 또한 우리 뷰티 철학의 중심에 있는 자유와 자신감, 자기표현을 드러내는 수단이 될 수 있다"고 말했다.

이 플랫폼은 멀티 플래티넘 음반 아티스트이자 메이블린 글로벌 앰배서더인 마일리 사이러 스 와 함께 시작한다. 사이러스의 활동 이력은 하나의 정체성에 갇히지 않고 다양한 가능성을 탐색하는 자유를 보여준다. 지난해 메이블린의 대표 슬로건에 목소리를 입힌 사이러스는 창의적인 변신을 거듭해 온 자신의 경력을 바탕으로 이제 슬로건에 담긴 새로운 의미를 알린다.

처음 대중의 주목을 받던 시절부터 오늘날의 아티스트가 되기까지, 사이러스는 저마다 고유한 사운드와 스타일, 관점을 지닌 뚜렷한 창작의 시기들을 거쳐 왔다. 메이크업은 각 시기마다 핵심적인 역할을 하며 다양한 스타일을 시도할 수 있게 해줬다. 각각의 스타일은 사이러스가 "이것이 지금의 나"라고 말하는 자신만의 방식이었다. 고유한 개성을 지키면서도 변화를 받아들이는 사이러스의 모습은 이번 캠페인의 앰배서더로서 자연스럽게 어울린다.

마일리 사이러스 메이블린 글로벌 앰배서더 는 "나는 '어쩌면.'을 모든 문이 열려 있다는 뜻으로 생각한다. 나 자신이 누구인지는 타고나는 것이지만, 자신에게 충실하다면 언제든 꿈꾸던 모습이 될 수 있다. 무한한 가능성은 누구에게나 있으며, 꿈꿀 수 있다면 실현할 수도 있다고 믿는다"고 말했다.

앞으로 수개월 동안 이 플랫폼은 음악계를 비롯한 다양한 분야에서 영감을 주는 여성들의 이야기를 통해 계속 확장될 예정이다. 이들은 가능성과 새로운 변화, 메이크업의 역할에 관한 각자의 관점을 전한다. 또한 개인적인 이야기와 경험을 통해 자신감과 자기표현이 어떻게 새로운 가능성으로 향하는 길을 열어주는지 보여주며, 다른 이들도 자신이 어떤 사람이 되고 싶은지 탐색하도록 영감을 줄 것이다. 이번 달 전 세계에 선보이는 이 플랫폼은 다양한 시도를 장려하는 혁신적인 제품과 창의성 및 자기표현을 기리는 협업, 캠페인을 통해 구체화된다.

새로운 브랜드 플랫폼에 관한 자세한 내용은 www.maybelline.com/maybe-were-born-with-it 에서 확인할 수 있다.

items.content:
글로벌뉴스 입력 :2026/11/11 00:10

자연어 처리로 추출한 새 임상 정보에 신뢰도 점수 부여…사람이 주석을 단 기록으로 검증하고 같은 비식별 환자의 구조화된 EHR 데이터와 연결

케임브리지, 매사추세츠 , 2026년 11월 10일 /PRNewswire/ -- 인공지능(AI)으로 임상기록에서 정보를 추출하는 일이 그 어느 때보다 쉬워지면서, 연구자에게 이제 더 어려운 질문은 그 데이터를 믿고 실사용 근거 생성에 활용해도 되는가가 됐다. 전 세계 연합형 의료 데이터 네트워크를 선도하는 트라이넷엑스(TriNetX®)가 임상 기록 NLP 추출 데이터(NLP-extracted Facts from Clinical Notes) 기능을 11월 10일 발표했다. 이 기능은 현재 TriNetX LIVE™ 플랫폼과 다운로드 가능한 데이터셋에서 이용할 수 있다. 연구자는 이 기능을 통해 8억 건이 넘는 임상기록과 보고서에서 추출한 즉시 분석 가능 데이터 항목을 확보할 수 있다. 기반 자료는 2026년 말까지 약 10억 건에 이를 것으로 예상된다.

임상기록에는 질병 병기와 전신수행상태, 바이오마커 검사 결과 등 구조화된 기록을 보완하는 세부 정보가 담겨 있지만, 이를 신뢰할 수 있게 추출하기는 어렵다. 트라이넷엑스는 AI와 심도 있는 임상 및 정보학 전문성을 결합해, 주석이 달린 대규모 표준 정답 기록으로 학습한 사람 참여형 처리 파이프라인을 구축한다. 트라이넷엑스는 추출 단계에서 끝나는 접근법과 달리, 사람이 주석을 단 기록으로 모든 파이프라인을 검증하고 각 정보에 신뢰도 점수를 부여한다. 또한 기록에서 추출한 데이터를 같은 비식별 환자의 구조화된 전자의무기록(EHR) 데이터와 연계해 연구자가 코호트를 확대하고 세밀하면서도 임상적으로 의미 있는 표현형을 구성할 수 있게 한다.

각 정보에는 다음 세 가지 검증 장치가 적용된다.

사람의 감독 . AI가 태그를 붙인 내용을 임상 전문가가 검토 및 수정하고, 모델은 수정 내용을 바탕으로 재학습한다. 각 모듈은 사람이 주석을 단 기록을 기준으로 정밀도 0.90 이상을 달성해야 한다.

임상적 확인 . 추출된 정보는 모델 지표뿐 아니라 예상되는 임상 양상과 비교해 검증한다. 예를 들어 추출된 미국 동부종양협력그룹(Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group, ECOG) 전신수행상태를 바탕으로 작성한 생존곡선에서는 점수가 2점 이상인 환자의 생존율이 더 낮게 나타났다.

지속적인 모니터링 . 트라이넷엑스는 새 의료기관이 임상기록 프로그램에 참여하고 새 기록 유형이 추가될 때 모델 성능을 모니터링하며, 변이가 나타나면 모델을 개선한다.

초기 결과에 따르면 기록에서 추출한 정보를 활용하면서 흡연 상태 정보 확보율이 22%에서 67%로 높아졌고, 폐암 코호트 연구에서 구조화된 데이터만 활용했을 때보다 6배 많은 환자를 확보했다. 또한 구조화된 필드에는 전신수행상태 정보가 전혀 없던 암 환자 29만 2000명에 대해 ECOG 및 카르노프스키 전신수행상태를 확인했다.

오거스트 캘훈(August Calhoun) 트라이넷엑스 CEO는 "AI에 의무기록을 분석하게 하는 일은 쉽다. 트라이넷엑스의 차별점은 그 방식에 있다. 우리는 데이터를 생성한 기관 내부에 데이터가 남아 있는 글로벌 연합형 네트워크에서 과학적 엄밀성과 인간의 전문성을 바탕으로 작업한다"며 "이는 AI가 일상적인 연구에 쓰이는 상황에서 임상기록이 엄격한 검증 통과의 근거가 될 수 있다는 뜻"이라고 말했다.

맷베이 팔추크(Matvey Palchuk) 트라이넷엑스 최고 의료정보학 책임자(MD, MS, FAMIA)는 "임상기록의 모든 세부 내용을 정확하면서도 의미 있게 추출할 수 있는 시스템은 없다. 이는 임상 언어의 본질에 내재한 한계"라며 "바로 그렇기 때문에 검증이 중요하다. 우리의 목표는 근거 생성에 신뢰하고 활용할 수 있는 정보를 추출하는 것"이라고 말했다.

임상 기록 NLP 추출 데이터는 현재 사회력(흡연, 음주 상태), 심장학, 호흡기학, 일반 종양학과 바이오마커, 간질환 등 다양한 영역을 포괄하며, 트라이넷엑스 네트워크 회원이 지금 이용할 수 있다. 자세한 내용은 trinetx.com/data/clinical-notes 에서 확인할 수 있다.

트라이넷엑스는 인류의 건강을 증진시켜 주는 글로벌 진실 엔진(The Global Truth Engine for Better Human Health®)이다. 20여개국, 1만 4200곳이 넘는 임상 현장을 연결하는 안전한 네트워크를 기반으로, 세계에서 가장 엄격한 과학적 검증도 통과할 수 있는 신뢰할 만한 근거를 제공하고 있다. 글로벌 데이터와 타협 없는 무결성, AI와 인간 지능의 보기 드문 융합을 결합해 발견을 촉진하고 전 세계에서 건강 지표의 개선을 이끌고 있다. 자세한 사항은 trinetx.com 을 참조하거나 링크드인(LinkedIn) 에서 트라이넷엑스를 팔로우하면 확인할 수 있다.

items.title: DeepMind reveals Gemini Robotics 2.5 and open safety benchmark "ASIMOV-jailbreak"
items.summary: The new model is up to twice as successful at some tasks.
items.content:
Google DeepMind has revealed a new generation of the AI-powered Gemini Robotics platform. In the 2.5 release, Google says its robotic AI is getting tantalizingly close to completing real-world tasks as well as humans do. In fact, some Gemini robots were able to get actual work done in Mercedes-Benz factories, and the team is preparing for a day when robots operate alongside humans with an open source safety benchmark.

DeepMind’s physical AI platform has several computational layers between user input and robotic action. There’s the vision-language model piece, which is Gemini Embodied Reasoning. Essentially, it takes your instructions and uses live video to plan how the robot can accomplish the task. The other main component is the vision-language-action (VLA) that actually generates robot actions, like moving an actuator—that’s Gemini Robotics, which has been bumped to version 2.5.

DeepMind says that Gemini Robotics 2.5 is much better at tasks that require a high degree of dexterity. The model was evaluated across more than 200 activities, including serving food with tongs and using a pipette, as you would see in a laboratory. Google also showed that Apptronik’s Apollo 2 humanoid robot with Gemini Robotics 2.5 can now tie a bow with its five-fingered hands, a notable feat, because deformable objects (like ribbon) are notoriously difficult for robots to manipulate.

Overall, Gemini Robotics 2.5 manages a 30 to 100 percent higher success rate compared to the last version . It’s also 20 to 30 percent faster. But that’s based on laboratory testing. Google partnered with Apptronik and Mercedes-Benz to see how capable this AI is when faced with the uncertainty of the world outside robotics labs. The Gemini-powered Apollo 2 robots kitted automotive parts in a few European factories, reaching a 96 percent success rate.

That’s an impressive showing compared to previous robotic AI systems, but it’s still probably not enough for a company like Mercedes-Benz. A human doing that sort of repetitive task will get it right virtually every time, and DeepMind director Kanishka Rao notes that closing that last 4 percent gap will be a “steep road.”

You could manually program a robot to do a handful of tasks in a factory without issue—this type of automation has been common for decades. Gemini Robotics is not trying to just do a few things, though. These are intended to be general robots that can handle almost anything, but there are trade-offs to that approach.

“We can be very good at a particular application at the cost of generalization,” said DeepMind Robotics head Carolina Parada. “Or we can just push on the generalization axis and maybe not get to 99.9 in every application.”

Training data is essential for training all generative AI models. Most text-based chatbots in existence were fed basically the entirety of the open Internet, but there isn’t as much “physical data” for robotic AI. The best kind of training data for robots comes from teleoperation, but the team says Gemini 4 Argon has helped create a “simulation engine” that greatly accelerated development of Gemini Robotics 2.5.

The team used Argon to generate thousands of variations on practice runs based on real-world camera data. These “digital twins” apparently allowed Gemini Robotics 2.5 to more quickly generalize new tasks and settings. There’s still a role for the real thing, though. DeepMind combined this synthetic data with traditional training demonstrations to ground the model.

Argon was also used for analyzing failures and suggesting ways to improve in both simulations and real robots. However, this isn’t something that works in real time. Frontier models like Gemini take time to churn through their tokens, but robots need to be able to operate without long pauses. The new VLA isn’t lightning quick, either. While Google has experimented with some embedded robotics models, the current 2.5 release is still running on cloud-based servers. So those gains in accuracy and speed still don’t come without latency. The video above is sped up by 2x to make the robot look more human-like.

DeepMind is also working to ensure the failures don’t put any nearby humans at risk. The team notes that Gemini Robotics 2.5 uses inference-time reasoning to avoid hazards. So if something gets in the way, the robot will stop completely or wait until it’s safe to continue. This is essential if you’re going to have a robot operating outside of the lab, for example, in a Mercedes factory. DeepMind says this feature allowed Gemini robots to safely complete tasks 33 percent more often when obstacles were present. The success rate went up 43 percent when people were in the way.

There is no agreed-upon way to test physical AI for safety, but DeepMind hopes to move the industry in that direction with ASIMOV-Jailbreak. This is an open source database that contains 1,500 prompts designed to trick a robotic AI into doing something unsafe. For example, a prompt might ask the robot to place items in a bag and close it with a fastener too fiddly for the robot to operate. The AI should decline to do that, but attempting to proceed and incorrectly closing the container would be the “unsafe” outcome.

DeepMind says that placing Argon in the loop results in a 98.8 percent jailbreak safety level. With just Gemini Robotics ER 2, the system scores 73.5 percent in Google’s safety benchmark.

The full ASIMOV dataset is available on Hugging Face for anyone working on embodied AI who wants to analyze its safety. Gemini Robotics 2.5 is not generally available, but it’s now in the hands of Google’s robotics partners, including Agile Robots, Apptronik, and Boston Dynamics.
